PROTECTION FROM VIOLENCE
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Palopo. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Palopo City which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Palopo City. 6. Regional Agency is the Regional Apparatus of Palopo City which includes the Regional Secretariat, Secretariat of the Regional People's Representative Council, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Administration is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 17. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 27.

5.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text does mention “lembaga adat” (customary institutions) in definitional/actor lists (Pasal 1 angka 13: penyelenggara includes “lembaga adat”; and Penjelasan Pasal 18 ayat (1) huruf d lists “lembaga adat” and “tokoh adat” as examples of “lembaga non pemerintah”). However, these passages only define who may be involved; they do not require or describe concrete engagement/consultation with traditional/cultural leaders in design/implementation (no mechanism, role, or activity is specified beyond being a possible non-government partner/implementer). If the indicator “Traditional/cultural engagement” expects explicit engagement actions (e.g., consultation, involvement in outreach, dispute resolution, program delivery), the judge over-interpreted mere inclusion in a definition as evidence of engagement. Thus the information was available, but the judge’s reasoning was too lenient.

PROTECTION FROM VIOLENCE
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Palopo. 2. Mayor is the Mayor of Palopo. 3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government which is the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Palopo City which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Palopo City. 6. Regional Agency is the Regional Apparatus of Palopo City which includes the Regional Secretariat, Secretariat of the Regional People's Representative Council, Regional Offices and Regional Technical Institutions. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict and the State. 9. Administration is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family members, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (drugs), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Implementer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing facilities needed for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 17. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 21. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 22. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 23. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 24. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is an institution providing services to victims of violence, which is hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution for recovery of victims of violence from the aspects of health, education and economic independence. 26. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 27.

Article 3
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is intended to provide protection and empowerment for women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER IX
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 20
(1) Regional Government is obligated to conduct development and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Development as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards.

Article 23
Regional Governments are obligated to allocate budget to P2TP2A in carrying out the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, and it shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 12
The Regional Government is obligated to provide a complaint unit for the protection of women and children who are victims of violence.

CHAPTER VI
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government in the context of providing protection services to women and children victims of violence, establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center.
(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children victims of violence.
(3) Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by a Mayor Regulation.

Article 2
Letter a The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).
Letter b The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter d The principle of the best interests of victims, that all actions concerning women and children are carried out by families, communities and Regional Governments to fulfill the rights of women and victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e

CHAPTER X
FINANCING
Article 22
Budget allocation for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Other lawful sources of income in accordance with Laws and Regulations;
c. Other sources of income that are non-binding in nature.

Article 16
Letter a What is meant by the right to have one's dignity respected is upholding human rights.
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by the right to obtain information is the right to obtain explanations, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with developments.
Letter e
Letter f What is meant by the victim's right to social rehabilitation, includes;
access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, citizenship.
Letter g What is meant by the right to compensation, includes; economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health and education or skills guarantees.
Letter h What is meant by the right to complaint handling is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter i Sufficiently clear.
Letter j What is meant by the right to assistance includes among others psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious leaders, advocates and family members.
What is meant by companion is an individual who works as a volunteer to provide protection and support to women and children who are victims of acts of violence during the judicial process, companions can come from family members, friends, or independent organizations that give attention to victims as well as advocates.

Article 19
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification/provision of information regarding women victims of violence; employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence whose education has been interrupted; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of an Agreement.

Article 21
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Mayor or to the DPRD.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PALOPO CITY
NUMBER 5 YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL.
Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household as well as outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and State. Therefore, the Palopo City Government is obligated to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, among others Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 Year 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Trafficking in Persons, and Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection.
The Regional Government prioritizes the implementation of Mandatory Government Affairs related to Basic Services as regulated in Article 11 paragraph (3) juncto Article 18 of Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government. The Basic Services referred to, one of which is empowerment and protection for women and children from acts of violence.
On that basis, the Palopo City Government has taken steps in order to provide protection to women and children victims of acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of society particularly to women and children. The causes among others are the still low understanding of society regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence to answer while at the same time providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from all forms of acts of violence that occur.
The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from actions to prevent acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government as well as the participation of the business community and society.
Our hope is that all forms of acts of violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Palopo City.

Article 8
The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters d and e are that they, by law, have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and to protect women and children as family members.

CHAPTER XI
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 24
(1) Officials appointed to organize integrated protection, integrated services and integrated recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations;
(2) Managers of P2TP2A duties who, in implementing protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles principles of organizing protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with P2TP2A internal mechanisms and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

6.1.rationale: The original Indonesian text defines “Korban” in Pasal 1 angka 8 as women and children experiencing violence “dalam situasi konflik, pasca konflik dan Negara” (in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the State). This is an explicit inclusion of conflict/post-conflict context for victims (including women). While “perlindungan khusus” in Pasal 1 angka 11 is framed for children, the indicator is about whether women in conflict/disaster areas are covered/recognized; the definition of victim already covers conflict/post-conflict situations for women. Since this relevant information was present in the retrieved candidates and supports a “Yes,” the golden label “Yes” is consistent with the text, and the judge’s “No” appears too strict; however the discrepancy is golden Yes vs predicted No, so the pipeline error is the judge decision. Still, because the judge rationale claims no explicit women-targeted measures, it may be applying a narrower standard than the golden. Given the indicator wording provided (“Women in conflict/disaster areas”), the policy does explicitly include conflict/post-conflict in the victim scope, so a “Yes” is defensible; the golden label does not appear wrong.
